summary: Seller training on handling customer cancellation claims in the Revibe orders app. A cancelled order shows a purple bar in the Orders list and a purple banner in the order drawer saying it is on hold. The seller must answer the cancellation claim by marking it valid (accept, refund and cancel) or invalid (reject). Marking invalid asks for a tracking ID, and a 24-hour ship obligation applies in some cases. Rules differ for UAE and South Africa, and Saudi Arabia. All 16 frames were opened. Several rules are garbled in the audio or conflict with the screen and are listed as unclear.

facts.statement: Two situations lead a customer to cancel an order: the customer changed his mind and no longer wants the device, or the shipment is delayed on the seller's side and the customer does not want to wait anymore.

evidence.quote: Basically, you will face two scenarios where a customer will cancel his order.
Either because he changed his mind, he doesn't want the device anymore.
{either?} because on your side the shipment is delayed and the customer doesn't want to wait anymore.

facts.statement: A cancellation claim has two answers. Accept marks the cancellation as valid (button labelled Mark valid). Reject marks the cancellation as invalid (button labelled Mark Invalid).

evidence.quote: Either you need to accept, so to mark the cancellation as being valid.
Either you reject, you mark the cancellation as being invalid.
Buttons: Mark valid, Mark Invalid, Mark Refunded, Cancel override

facts.statement: If the seller does not respond within 24 hours after the order has been {we?}, the claim is treated as marked valid. The order is then cancelled and the customer is refunded. The starting point of the 24 hours is not confirmed (see unclear).

evidence.quote: Please note that without a response from your side within 24 hours after the order has been {we?}
will consider that you mark it valid and that the order will then be cancelled and the customer
will be refunded.

facts.statement: Marking a cancellation as valid refunds the customer and cancels the order.

evidence.quote: So basically, if you accept,
the customer will be refunded and the order will be cancelled.

facts.statement: For UAE and South Africa orders, when the order is at the stage the audio reads as '{created?}', the seller must always mark the cancellation as valid. The stage name is unreliable (see unclear).

evidence.quote: Please note also that for UAE and South Africa, when the order is at {created?} stage, you always
have to mark the cancellation as being valid.

facts.statement: For UAE and South Africa orders at the quality check stage, the seller may mark the cancellation as invalid (reject it).

evidence.quote: So {for?} UAE and South Africa, you can mark the order as being invalid when it's at quality
check stage.

facts.statement: When a cancellation is rejected (marked invalid) for a UAE or South Africa order at the quality check stage, the seller must ship the order within the next 24 hours.

evidence.quote: In this situation, you can reject the cancellation, but you will have to ship the order within the
next 24 hours.

facts.statement: For Saudi Arabia orders, the seller always has the option to reject the cancellation, but must then ship the order within the next 24 hours.

evidence.quote: For Saudi Arabia orders, you will always have the option to reject the cancellation, {but?} you will also
have to ship it within the next 24 hours.

facts.statement: Marking a claim as invalid requires a tracking ID. Without one, the system shows the error 'Tracking ID is required to mark the claim as invalid' and opens an 'Add tracking ID' modal with a Tracking ID field and Cancel and Add buttons. Which countries require it is unclear (see unclear).

asr_fixes.basis: The company name in the screen URL (stage-admin.revibe.me, frame t00000.jpg), which matches Revibe.

unclear.issue: The start of the 24-hour window is garbled: 'within 24 hours after the order has been {we?}'. The screen shows a 'Since creation' counter on the claim and a Confirmed Date in the list, but the frames do not confirm which event starts the clock. Do not state the trigger as fact.
The stage name for the always-valid rule for UAE and South Africa is marked {created?}. No frame shows the stage list, so the exact stage name is unconfirmed.

Tracking ID scope conflicts. The narration says 'This you will have to do it for Saudi Arabia orders only' at 02:23, and the sentence about UAE and South Africa is incomplete ('{for?} UAE and South Africa orders.' at 02:28). The order on screen is a United Arab Emirates order (Country field, frame t00044.jpg), and the system shows 'Tracking ID is required to mark the claim as invalid' (frame t00139.jpg). Which countries require a tracking ID cannot be determined from the evidence.
'tracking ID link' is unclear. It may mean the tracking ID field or a tracking link, and the screen does not show it.

The result of marking invalid is not shown. Frames t00167.jpg, t00187.jpg and t00202.jpg still show Stage 'To be cancelled' and Status 'Open' on the claim. Whether the purple banner disappears and the order becomes editable is not confirmed on screen.

The word {cannot?} is marked low confidence. The narration 'you cannot do anything' is clear, but the screen shows only greyed-out fields and an Edit button, so the editing restriction rests on narration.
Mark Refunded (greyed out) and Cancel override are on screen but not explained by the trainer. Their purpose and when they apply are unknown.
Gross sale and Order amount show 399 with no currency on screen. The currency is not confirmed.
The closing sentence is garbled ('I remanage your disposal {may?} you have any further {question.?}'). It is not a usable fact.

outdated.signal: The trainer says the policy was 'just launched' but gives no launch date. The policy and this video may age without a visible date.

Sample data is inconsistent with its dates. The claim date is 2025-05-19 and the order was confirmed 19/05/2025, yet the banner says 'on hold (about 1 hour ago)' and Since creation shows 0 Day(s), 0 Hour(s). Today is 2026-10-22, so the timers and dates in the frames are not representative.
The screens come from the staging admin (stage-admin.revibe.me), so the layout, buttons and labels may differ in the live admin.
